nodes.name: Proposition 3.4: for $\mathsf{BFC}_{(X,Y,Z;H)}$
nodes.statement:
Given a bipartite graph $H\subseteq K_{X,Y}$ and a subset $Z\subseteq X$. There exists an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{BFC}_{(X,Y,Z; H)}$ such that any critical set $\sigma$ satisfies 
		\[|\sigma|\leq 2|Y|+|Z| + |H|.\]
		Moreover, the inequality is strict whenever $H$ contains at least one edge.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.5, Lemma 2.6: Join Projection
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with partition $E=E_1\cup \cdots \cup E_m$ and for every $i$, let $\mathsf{F}_i\subseteq 2^{E_i}$ be a non-empty subfamily. Suppose $\mathcal{M}_i$ is an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{F}_i$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_i \subseteq \mathsf{F}_i$.
		Then
		there exists an acyclic matching 
		on the join $\mathsf{F}_1 * \cdots * \mathsf{F}_m$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_1 * \cdots * \mathsf{U}_m$. In particular, if one of the $\mathcal{M}_i$ is complete, then $\mathsf{F}$ has a complete acyclic matching.

Let $E$ be a finite set with partition $E=\bigcup_{i\in I}E_i$ and let $\pi:2^E \to 2^I$ be the corresponding projection map. 
		Given a set $\tau\subseteq E$ and a family $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq 2^I$, define the family $\mathsf{F} = \{\sigma\subseteq E : \pi(\sigma)\in \mathsf{Q}, \tau\subseteq \sigma\}$. Then the following are true:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item  $\pi(\mathsf{F})=\{\overline{\sigma}\in \mathsf{Q} : \pi(\tau)\subseteq \overline{\sigma}\}$. 
			\item  Suppose $\pi(\mathsf{F})$ has an acyclic matching $\mathcal{M}_{\pi(\mathsf{F})}$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_{\pi(\mathsf{F})}$. Then 
			there exists an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{F}$ 
			with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_F$, such that the restriction $\pi: \mathsf{U}_F \to \mathsf{U}_{\pi(F)}$ is an injection where $|\sigma|=|\pi(\sigma)|-|\pi(\tau)|+|\tau|$ for every $\sigma \in U_F$.
		\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Lemma 2.5: Join
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with partition $E=E_1\cup \cdots \cup E_m$ and for every $i$, let $\mathsf{F}_i\subseteq 2^{E_i}$ be a non-empty subfamily. Suppose $\mathcal{M}_i$ is an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{F}_i$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_i \subseteq \mathsf{F}_i$.
		Then
		there exists an acyclic matching 
		on the join $\mathsf{F}_1 * \cdots * \mathsf{F}_m$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_1 * \cdots * \mathsf{U}_m$. In particular, if one of the $\mathcal{M}_i$ is complete, then $\mathsf{F}$ has a complete acyclic matching.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.6: Projection
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set with partition $E=\bigcup_{i\in I}E_i$ and let $\pi:2^E \to 2^I$ be the corresponding projection map. 
		Given a set $\tau\subseteq E$ and a family $\mathsf{Q}\subseteq 2^I$, define the family $\mathsf{F} = \{\sigma\subseteq E : \pi(\sigma)\in \mathsf{Q}, \tau\subseteq \sigma\}$. Then the following are true:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item  $\pi(\mathsf{F})=\{\overline{\sigma}\in \mathsf{Q} : \pi(\tau)\subseteq \overline{\sigma}\}$. 
			\item  Suppose $\pi(\mathsf{F})$ has an acyclic matching $\mathcal{M}_{\pi(\mathsf{F})}$ with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_{\pi(\mathsf{F})}$. Then 
			there exists an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{F}$ 
			with collection of critical sets $\mathsf{U}_F$, such that the restriction $\pi: \mathsf{U}_F \to \mathsf{U}_{\pi(F)}$ is an injection where $|\sigma|=|\pi(\sigma)|-|\pi(\tau)|+|\tau|$ for every $\sigma \in U_F$.
		\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 3.2: for $\mathsf{FC}_{H}$
nodes.statement:
Given a graph $H\subseteq K_V$ where  $|V|$ is odd. There exists an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{FC}_{H}$ such that any critical set $\sigma$ satisfies 
		\[|\sigma|\leq \textstyle{\frac{3}{2}}(|V|-1)+|H|.\]
		Moreover, the inequality is strict whenever $H$ contains at least one edge.

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1: for $\mathsf{PM}_{H}$
nodes.statement:
Given a graph $H\subseteq K_V$ where $|V|$ is even. There exists an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{PM}_H$ such that any critical set $\sigma$ satisfies 
		\[|\sigma| \leq \textstyle{\frac{3}{2}}|V| +|H|.\]
		Moreover, the inequality is strict whenever $V$ is non-empty.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement:
There is an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{F}_H$ such that any critical set $\sigma$ satisfies 
		\[|\sigma| \leq 3k-4+|H|.\]

nodes.name: Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement:
There is an acyclic matching on $\mathsf{B}_H$ such that any critical set $\sigma$ satisfies 
		\[|\sigma| \leq 2k-3+|H|.\]

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set and $\mathsf{K}\subseteq 2^E$ be a simplicial complex. And let $H_i(\mathsf{K})$ be the homology of $\mathsf{K}$ with coefficients in a fixed field $\mathbb{F}$. Suppose that there is an acyclic matching $\mathcal{M}$ on $\mathsf{K} \setminus \{\emptyset \}$. Then for every $i\geq 0$,
		$\dim H_i(\mathsf{K})$ is at most the number of critical sets with respect to $\mathcal{M}$ of dimension $i$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2: for $K_V$
nodes.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer and $G$ a graph.
		The link of any non-empty face of the complex $\mathsf{NM}_k(G)$ has vanishing homology in all dimensions $d\geq 3k-4$. Moreover, if $G$ is bipartite, then the link of any non-empty face of the complex $\mathsf{NM}_k(G)$ has vanishing homology in all dimensions $d\geq 2k-3$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.7
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathsf{K}$ be a simplicial complex on the vertex set $V$ which satisfies property {\em ($\ast$)}.
		Then, for any non-empty subset $S\subseteq V$, the induced subcomplex $\mathsf{K}[S]$ also satisfies property {\em ($\ast$)}.

nodes.name: Corollary 4.8
nodes.statement: Let $\mathsf{K}$ be a simplicial complex on the vertex set $V$ which satisfies property {\em ($\ast$)}. Then $\mathsf{K}$ has vanishing homology in all dimension $d\geq d_0+1$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: Let $k\geq 2$ be an integer and $G$ a graph. The complex $\mathsf{NM}_k(G)$ has vanishing homology in all dimensions $d\geq 3k-3$. Moreover, if $G$ is bipartite, then $\mathsf{NM}_k(G)$ has vanishing homology in all dimensions $d\geq 2k-2$.
